properties.areaDesc: Columbia River Bar
properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 5 at 8:41PM PDT until October 6 at 12:00PM PDT by NWS Portland OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Dense Fog Advisory, dense fog will reduce
visibility to 1 NM or less. For the Small Craft Advisory, rough
bar conditions expected. Seas 4 to 5 ft at 11 seconds and north
winds 15 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25 kt expected.

* WHERE...In the Main Channel of the Columbia River Bar.

* WHEN...Dense Fog Advisory, until noon PDT Tuesday. Small Craft
Advisory, from 5 PM Tuesday to 2 AM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the
Columbia River Bar. Low visibility will make navigation
difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Ebb current of 4.85 kt at 233 AM Wednesday.
Seas 5 ft.
properties.instruction:
A Small Craft Advisory means that wave conditions are expected to
be hazardous to small craft in the vicinity of the Columbia River
Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

If you must navigate, proceed with caution. Use proper fog
signals. Make sure all running lights are on. Remember to use
your radar and compass.

properties.areaDesc: Gadsden, FL
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 11:06PM EDT until October 6 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Gadsden County in Big Bend Florida...

* Until 200 AM EDT.

* At 1106 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the
warned area. Between 6 and 9 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Quincy, Midway, Havana, Greensboro, Gretna, Santa Clara, Quincy
Airport, Douglas City, Littman, Shady Rest, Sawdust, Florence,
Wetumpka, Dogtown, Branchville, Mount Pleasant, Freemont, Jamieson
and Hardaway.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
